title: Classify PR commits by content in pr_commits, not Athena-Job trailers
summary: Rewrite `pr_commits` in land.rs to classify each commit in `remote_base..head` by its content. The goal is that `athena land --pr` stops refusing real pull requests. The audience is Sri and the verifier, who run the athena-core land and gh tests. The caller in gh.rs passes each commit's kind through instead of hard-coding JobLanding.

defaults_applied.how: New classification and refusal tests; clippy and fmt checks.
Criteria check the kinds produced for a realistic range and the sha in the refusal error.
Trailer reliance is removed entirely instead of adding exceptions.
The change is confined to land.rs and its caller in gh.rs.
The behavior criteria name the cargo test commands the verifier can run.
Only Rust code and tests change.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: LandingCommit.kind and validation already exist in athena-data (b6f22c2), so athena-data does not change.

A job's closing records are recognised by paths added under records/jobs/<month>/<job>/ for the candidate, verification and outcome. I did not confirm the exact file names, so the producer must read how they are written.
The verification id comes from the existing `verification_id(job, commit)` in gh.rs.
A commit is compared against its first parent. Merge commits are not expected in a PR range.
Ordering of the checks: unchanged fingerprint first, then intervention record added, then job closing records, otherwise refuse.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`. A test builds a range shaped like this repo's real PRs: reading, dispatch and introspection commits (records only), a lease commit under operator/, an intervention commit adding records/interventions/<month>/<id>.json, then a job's landing commit adding its candidate, verification and outcome records. No commit carries an Athena-Job trailer. The test passes and asserts kinds in order: records_only for the first four, declared_intervention, then job_landing with that job and the verification id.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`. A refusal test adds a commit that changes governed content without being an intervention or a job's closing records. `pr_commits` returns an error that contains that commit's sha.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh::`. The gh tests still pass, and the commits built for a Landing record carry the kind from `pr_commits` and pass `LandingCommit::validate`.
`pr_commits` and `PrCommit` no longer read trailers or mention Athena-Job. `PrCommit` carries the kind, plus an optional job and verification. The doc comments describe the content rules.
A commit is records_only when its fingerprint equals its parent's, using the same `fingerprint(git, commit, base)` function the gate invariant uses. An empty range is still an error.
The old trailer-count tests for `pr_commits` are removed or replaced, not left alongside the new behavior.
Run `cargo clippy -p athena-core --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.

out_of_scope: Changing the Landing record schema or LandingKind.
Running the full workspace test suite.
departures: The previous attempt at this fix hit the 1800s deadline, so cost and time are raised a little and the pass probability lowered. Building a realistic git range test is slow.
